Documentation → Plugin Studio: build your own → Your first view

Your first view, step by step

A complete tutorial — build a "Policies per device" view with a device filter, preview it, move it through testing and publish it to Custom Views, explaining every line on the way.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio
📍 WherePlugins → Report Studio → New view (URL /plugins/new)
On this page
  • What you will build
  • Step 1 — open Report Studio
  • Step 2 — name it
  • Step 3 — pick the data
  • Step 4 — add a device filter
  • Step 5 — write the body
  • Step 6 — preview
  • Step 7 — save, test, publish
  • Step 8 — make it yours
  • Next

What you will build#

A view called Policies per device: a device selector at the top, a count of server policies, and a table of the policies of the chosen device with their virtual server, pool, WAF profile and status — coloured badges for enabled and disabled. About 15 minutes.

📌Required

You need studio.plugin_studio and a device ADOM with at least one FortiWeb whose configuration SATOM has synced (the view reads the cached server policies). Work in the FortiWeb ADOM.

Step 1 — open Report Studio#

  1. In the FortiWeb ADOM, go to Plugins → Report Studio.
  2. Click New view. The editor opens with a Definition card on the left and a Sandboxed preview on the right. The view is stamped with the ADOM you are in: only this ADOM will see it.

Step 2 — name it#

Field Value Why
Name Policies per device What people see in Custom Views
Kind view A full page (a widget is a tile)
Icon bi-shield-check Any Bootstrap icon name, bi-…

Step 3 — pick the data#

Under Datasets (read-only), type server in the search box and tick Server policies (rich) (server_policies_full). Then tick Fleet appliances (fleet_appliances) under Built-in.

  • server_policies_full gives one row per cached server policy: device, policy, vserver, server_pool, wpp, status, traffic_log, comment, appid and more.
  • fleet_appliances gives one row per device: id, name, kind, firmware, host, port.

Both arrive already cut to the person who opens the view: only their ADOM's devices. You never write SQL. (The list holds hundreds of datasets — see Datasets for what each source is.)

Step 4 — add a device filter#

Under Inputs, click Add input and fill in:

Field Value
Name device
Label Device
Type Device
required unticked

A Device input shows the viewer a list of the devices they may see. Its value reaches the body as params.device — the device id, as text, or empty when nothing is chosen.

Step 5 — write the body#

Paste this into Body (Jinja / HTML):

{# 1. the rows of the chosen device, or every row when none is chosen #}
{% set rows = server_policies_full.rows %}
{% if params.device %}
  {% set rows = rows | selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", params.device) | list %}
{% endif %}

<div class="fw-card">
  <div class="fw-card-header">
    <h2 class="fw-card-title">Server policies — {{ rows | length }}</h2>
  </div>
  <div class="fw-card-body">
    {% if rows %}
    <div class="fw-table-wrapper">
      <table class="fw-table">
        <thead><tr><th>Device</th><th>Policy</th><th>Virtual server</th>
                   <th>Pool</th><th>WAF profile</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
        {% for p in rows | sort(attribute="policy") %}
          <tr>
            <td>{{ p.device }}</td>
            <td><code>{{ p.policy }}</code></td>
            <td>{{ p.vserver }}</td>
            <td>{{ p.server_pool or "—" }}</td>
            <td>{{ p.wpp or "none" }}</td>
            <td>
              {% if p.status == "enable" %}<span class="fw-badge fw-badge-success">enabled</span>
              {% else %}<span class="fw-badge fw-badge-secondary">{{ p.status or "unknown" }}</span>{% endif %}
            </td>
          </tr>
        {% endfor %}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    {% else %}
      <p class="fw-muted">No cached server policy for this choice.</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</div>

What each part does:

  • {% set rows = server_policies_full.rows %} — a dataset is a variable named by its key, with .rows (a list of dicts) and .columns.
  • selectattr("appliance_id", "equalto", params.device) keeps the rows of the chosen device. Built-in datasets hand values over as text (the appliance_id is "7", not 7), which is why comparing with the text of params.device works.
  • sort(attribute="policy"), length, or "—" — ordinary Jinja filters and operators. See Writing views for the full toolbox.
  • fw-card, fw-table, fw-badge-success come from SATOM's class kit: no CSS needed, and the view follows the customer's theme.

Step 6 — preview#

Click Live preview. The right side renders the unsaved body with the real data, for you. Choose a device in the preview's Device list to see the filter work.

If a red Plugin render error card appears, read its message: it names the problem (an unknown variable, a missing endif…). See Troubleshooting.

Step 7 — save, test, publish#

  1. Click Save. The view is a draft: only holders of studio.plugin_studio can open it.
  2. In Lifecycle, click Promote to Testing and look at the preview once more.
  3. Click Promote to Published. SATOM renders the saved body one more time; if it fails, publishing is refused with the error.

Everyone signed in to the FortiWeb ADOM now finds Policies per device under Plugins → Custom Views, each of them seeing only their own devices.

Step 8 — make it yours#

  • Add traffic_log as a column and a badge when it is disable.
  • Add a Select input status with options enable|Enabled and disable|Disabled, and filter on p.status == params.status.
  • Replace server_policies_full with the device-object dataset fortiweb_server_policy to show any field FortiWeb keeps for a policy (up to 125 columns) — its appliance_id is a number, so compare with params.device | int.
  • Export it (Export) and import it on another SATOM — see Test and publish.

Next#

  • Datasets: the data a view reads — what else you can read, including FortiGate, FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer objects.
  • Writing views — loops, grouping, totals, charts in JavaScript.
  • Recipes — finished views to copy.
